client: python-httpx language-neutral probe (not a native client)
environment: local lane Supabase stack argus-native-auth-proof (jwt_expiry=60, confirmations on) + unchanged Argus API; Argus API launched from the fix branch at argus_api_head

results.scenario: Argus /auth/login with no Origin and no cookies returns the session in JSON
results.expected: 200 with access_token, refresh_token, expires_in; user id
results.note: Argus also sets sb-auth-token and sb-refresh-token cookies; a bearer client must not store them.

results.scenario: Bearer access token reaches a harmless protected endpoint (GET /me)
results.expected: 200 and the profile email matches the signed-in user

results.scenario: No bearer and no cookie is rejected
Refresh directly against Supabase Auth with the public anon key, as the web does
results.expected: 200, rotated refresh token, same session_id; Argus accepts the new access token
results.note: The previous access token stays usable until its exp because the session row is unchanged.

results.scenario: Five unserialized refreshes with one refresh token inside the reuse window
results.expected: Server tolerates reuse inside refresh_token_reuse_interval (10 s locally)
results.note: The reuse window hides races only when every racer finishes inside it.

results.scenario: Late racers present older refresh tokens after the reuse window
results.expected: Record Supabase's rule: which older tokens are still accepted, and whether the family is revoked
results.note: A token two rotations old is refused; the immediate parent is tolerated. One lost refresh response is survivable, two are a sign-out. Clients single-flight refresh and persist the rotated token before using it.

results.scenario: Expired access token is rejected; refresh recovers without re-entering credentials
results.expected: 401 unauthorized on the expired token, then 200 after refresh
results.note: Another account signed in through the same API process afterwards, which moves that process's server-side refresh timer off this session (see A14). The API does not distinguish expired from revoked; clients refresh once on 401 and treat a second 401 as signed out.

results.scenario: The client alone owns refresh for a session Argus issued (the most recent sign-in on this API process, left untouched)
results.expected: The client's refresh token is still valid after the access token expires
results.note: Failed assumption. Argus's shared server-side supabase-py auth client keeps the last session it signed in and refreshes it on a timer (auto_refresh_token defaults to true), rotating the token the client holds. Once it rotates twice, the client's token is refused and the user is signed out. Affects web and native alike.

results.scenario: Argus POST /auth/logout alone (clearing local state only)
results.expected: 200, but the same access token still works: nothing was revoked
results.note: Discarding tokens locally leaves a live refresh token server-side. Native logout must revoke.

results.scenario: Supabase signOut(scope: local) revokes this session; Argus rejects its unexpired access token
results.expected: 204; /me 401 before the JWT exp; refresh token rejected
results.note: Argus checks auth.sessions on every request, so revocation is immediate, not at token expiry.

results.scenario: Sign out other devices, then everywhere
results.expected: others: this device 200, tablet 401; global: this device 401

results.scenario: The server resolves identity only from the bearer on each request
results.expected: Each token returns its own user; switching is a client-side cache and in-flight concern

results.scenario: A platform-default cookie store keeps Argus's sb-auth-token from the last /auth/login
results.expected: Failed assumption: a request that omits the bearer is silently authenticated as the cookie's user
results.note: Bearer takes precedence, but any code path that forgets the header acts as the previous account. Native clients must not keep sb-* cookies.

results.scenario: Argus login attempt limit versus calling Supabase password sign-in directly
results.expected: Argus answers 401 for 8 attempts, then 429 with Retry-After; direct Supabase calls are not counted by Argus
results.note: Direct SDK sign-in skips Argus's limiter, allowlist gate, profile repair, and guest claim. Sign-in stays on Argus.

results.scenario: A non-allowlisted account signs in directly against Supabase
results.expected: Argus login 401; direct Supabase issues a session; Argus still refuses it on every product call
results.note: The allowlist is enforced twice, so a direct session is not an access bypass, but it is a live Supabase session Argus never counted.
